newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish judge seeks U.S. spy files on Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Spanish judge seeks U.S. spy files on Argentina.

text.p: A Spanish High Court judge has asked the United States to hand over all its intelligence files on Argentina's 1976-83 military dictatorship, court documents published on Wednesday said.

Judge Baltasar Garzon, who is investigating the disappearance of Spaniards during Argentina's dictatorship, requested papers via an international commission from the CIA, the FBI, the Pentagon and U.S. embassies in Latin America.

In the February 28 court order, Garzon said he was seeking all data available on: "The start of the military repression and the paramilitary forces in Argentina that had as a consequence the death and disappearance of 330 Spanish citizens and Spanish descendants residing in that country".

The judge, who has called on 101 members of the Argentine armed forces to give evidence about the "dirty war" in which thousands disappeared without a trace, reiterated that request and asked Spain to take measures to ensure they appear.

Garzon said Argentine authorities had violated a treaty with Spain on judicial cooperation that the two countries had ratified in 1990 and the South American country had a "legal obligation" to comply with his court's requests.
"They have decided that a blanket of ominous silence will cover up what happened forever," Garzon said in another court document. "It's a cruel reality."
